clue.text: Beginning to threaten song after the wee small hours? It must be the liqueur

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of threaten
one o'clock in the morning, 1 AM, with the 1 read as the letter I
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A late-night drinker starts belting out songs after midnight, and blames the after-dinner drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the song behind the hour: TIA MARIA. '1 AM' as I AM is a playful letter-for-digit swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee-flavoured liqueur from Jamaica.

clue.text: Times editor getting rubbed out

parts.note: eras are periods of history, times
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor of The Times newspaper is murdered, or at least removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Times' look like the newspaper, but it is just periods of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rubbed out with an eraser has been deleted, the past participle matching 'rubbed out'.

clue.text: Steal dog and lizard

parts.note: to whip is slang for to steal
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with someone's dog and their pet lizard too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like a noun beside 'Steal', but it is the verb meaning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiptail is a kind of American lizard named for its long slender tail.

clue.text: People often emulated that man and revolted, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: that man is he, and to revolt is to rise, so he rose

explanation.surface: Someone admired and copied turns out to have led a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroes are role models, people whom others admire and try to imitate.

clue.text: Earlier term for monastery or other religious building

parts.note: prior means earlier

indicators.note: a term is an end point, so only the closing letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of monastery

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned word that once meant monastery or some other church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier term for' reads like an etymology note; in fact 'term' picks the last letter of monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a religious house run by a prior or prioress, smaller than an abbey.

clue.text: Secure one working cogwheel

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or secure
Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An instruction to fasten a single working gear in a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinion is a small toothed gear that meshes with a larger wheel or rack.

clue.text: Tense anger about King's ultimatum

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: heat is passion or anger
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch's furious final demand creates a tense atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like a mood adjective, but it is the grammar abbreviation; R for Rex is the usual crossword king.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a final demand backed by a threat of punishment if refused.

clue.text: One has three legs? That'll be the consequences of taking drugs

parts.note: two results of drug use are listed in turn
a trip is a hallucinatory drug experience
OD is short for overdose

explanation.surface: A joke about a three-legged creature being the result of drug use.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical definition: a camera stand, not a mutant animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand for a camera or telescope, hence it has three legs.

clue.text: Leaf collector, or artisan working with tree

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked over and reshaped into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who gathers fallen leaves, or a craftsman shaping wood from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf collector' suggests autumn gardening; the leaves are tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer catches the loose tea leaves as the tea is poured.

clue.text: Problem in America backing hostile stance

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the letters run from right to left

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
taken as written
A is an abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A troublesome issue in the US supports an aggressive attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus is ill will or hostility toward someone, a hostile attitude.

clue.text: Ecstatic feeling reversed unparalleled regret after consuming noodle soup

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one string is taken inside another
reversed tells us the next two items are read from end to start

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I
to rue is to regret
pho is a Vietnamese noodle soup

explanation.surface: Delight turns to regret after eating a bowl of noodle soup.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 + RUE reversed gives EURIA, which then takes in PHO: EU(PHO)RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a state of intense happiness or elation.

clue.text: Animal cry beginning to resound over a river

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of resound
O for over, as in cricket scoring
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A beast's call begins to echo across the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A roar is the loud deep call of a lion or similar big animal.

clue.text: Calm debate has father overruling copper

indicators.note: to overrule is to set aside one ruling in favour of another, so one element displaces another

parts.note: a discussion is a debate
pa is an informal word for father
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: In a family argument, dad pulls rank over a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal, symbol Cu, which PA replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispassion is calmness, freedom from strong emotion or bias.

clue.text: Lawless people who may be found climbing rocky brutal crags

definitions.text: Lawless people who may be found climbing rocky brutal crags

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the following letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Outlaws scrambling over harsh rocky cliffs, perhaps in a hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, with the anagram tucked into its last three words: these villains climb walls rather than crags.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat burglars are thieves who climb up walls and drainpipes to break into buildings.

clue.text: Sibling about to get upset stomach, mostly from vegetable

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bro is short for brother
C for circa, about
colic is a stomach upset

explanation.surface: A brother is about to fall ill with a tummy upset from eating greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is part of the surface, linking the brother to his upset stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Broccoli is a green vegetable of the cabbage family eaten for its flower heads.

clue.text: Prayer allowance about to proceed heavenwards

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

indicators.note: in a down entry, going heavenwards means reading upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: A permitted prayer is about to rise up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'on the point of' in the surface but signals wrapping; heavenwards works only because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogation is a solemn prayer of supplication, especially on the Rogation Days before Ascension.

clue.text: Wretched person who's joined religious movement?

parts.note: someone who has joined a group is in it
a sect is a religious movement

explanation.surface: A miserable soul who has signed up to a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'who's joined religious movement' is read as IN SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect is a contemptuous term for a small, worthless or despicable person.

clue.text: US University coming in to repudiate ignoring Democratic opposition

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one word goes inside another
ignoring means leaving out, so the letter named is dropped

parts.note: to deny is to repudiate
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: An American university rejects the Democrats' opposing stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as US politics, but Democratic just supplies a single letter to be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility or mutual opposition between parties.

clue.text: Hostility? A good man is not provoked

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is there hostility? A decent man doesn't rise to provocation.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonism is active opposition or hostility between people.

clue.text: Variation in maths and algebra finally leading to complaint

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters appear in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of algebra

explanation.surface: Struggling with different maths and algebra ends up making a student ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' here is a medical one, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory condition, and complaint can mean an illness or ailment.

clue.text: The writer's uplifting story, linked to high-class environment

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and the writer's is short for I'm
a story can be a lie
U means upper-class

explanation.surface: An author's inspiring tale is tied to an upmarket setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer's = I'M, turned upwards to MI, then LIE and U: MI + LIE + U.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's social surroundings or environment.

clue.text: Signal information for racing fraternity I overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: the going is the state of the ground, vital to horse racing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racing tip-off is a signal someone missed.
explanation.walkthrough: The going, reported as good, soft or firm, tells punters about track conditions in British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A gong is struck as a signal, for example to call people to dinner.

clue.text: Line secured by camping expert? It often flaps about

parts.note: a tent is what you camp in

indicators.note: secured by means held in place by, so one element sits inside the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A guy rope fixed by an expert camper keeps flapping in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camping expert' must be split into two words, and the line sits inside the second one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentacle is a flexible limb of an octopus or squid that waves about.

clue.text: Country set in mostly established area

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other
mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: laid as in established, like laid foundations
a TV set
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A nation is placed largely within a settled region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a verb meaning placed, but it is a noun: a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic country between Estonia and Lithuania.

clue.text: Critical comment about Scottish island — no end to that uproar

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval

indicators.note: no end means losing the last letter of the item just named

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone tuts about a Hebridean island and the noise never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is an island off the west coast of Scotland; 'that' refers back to the island, which loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumult is a loud confused noise, as of a crowd, synonymous with uproar.

clue.text: Supplementary ROM eminently embodies this, on reflection?

definitions.text: Supplementary ROM eminently embodies this, on reflection?

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters run backwards
embodies means contains within its body, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Extra read-only memory is the perfect example of this thing, if you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: extra ROM is computer memory, and the reversed hidden word is that very thing.
explanation.definitionFit: ROM is read-only memory, so supplementary ROM is more computer memory.
